q: An adjacency list for V nodes and E edges uses…
why: Each node has a list; each edge appears once (twice if undirected).

q: What does an adjacency matrix do faster than a list?
options: Check if a specific edge (u, v) exists

q: Building an adjacency list from an UNDIRECTED edge [a, b]…
why: Undirected means you can travel either way.

q: An undirected graph has 7 edges. What's the sum of all node degrees?
why: Every edge contributes 1 to each of its two endpoints: 2E.

q: The town judge in a directed trust graph has…
why: Trusted by everyone else, trusts nobody.

q: A 2D grid of land and water. How do you treat it as a graph?
options: Each cell is a node; its up/down/left/right cells are its neighbours
Build a matrix of all pairs
why: An implicit graph: no need to build the adjacency list at all.
